statement: A rectangular card measures 20 cm by 14 cm. A 3 cm by 3 cm square is cut from each corner, and the four flaps are folded up to make an open box. What is the volume of the box, in cubic centimetres?

choices.misconception: I found the area of the base, 14 x 8, and forgot to multiply by the height of 3.
I worked out the area of card left after cutting, 280 - 36, instead of the volume.
I took 3 off each length only once, getting a base of 17 by 11, though a square is cut at both ends.
I multiplied 20 x 14 x 3 as if no corners had been cut away.

hints: What are the length, width and height of the folded box?
Each corner cut removes 3 cm from both ends of every side, so each base edge shrinks twice. The height of the box is the size of the cut. Multiply the three dimensions.
The base is 20 - 6 = 14 cm by 14 - 6 = 8 cm, and the box is 3 cm tall.

solutions.reliable: Cutting a 3 cm square from both ends of the 20 cm side leaves 20 - 6 = 14 cm, and the 14 cm side becomes 14 - 6 = 8 cm. The flaps fold up to a height of 3 cm. The volume is 14 x 8 x 3 = 336 cubic cm. The transferable idea: before computing, picture the folded solid and read each of its dimensions off the flat net.

whyOnTest: Folding a net into a box checks that you can see which flat lengths become which edges, and the traps are cutting only one end or reporting an area.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
